experiments.hypothesis: Software vendors will pay repeatedly to avoid owning EUDR submission and reconciliation failures.
experiments.method: Interview 10 integration owners, run 5 ACCEPTANCE fixtures, request a paid design-partner commitment.
experiments.pass: At least 1 paid partner or 2 written procurement-intent commitments plus a real failing fixture.
experiments.kill: Direct API maintenance is consistently reported as trivial and no buyer will provide a fixture or budget.

experiments.hypothesis: eFTI platform/TMS vendors need independent pre-certification regression tests.
experiments.method: 10 technical interviews, 3 prototype runs, request one sample schema and one paid/prepaid pilot.
experiments.pass: Three run the prototype, one contributes a sample, and one pays or prepays.
experiments.kill: Certification bodies or official tooling provide a complete free suite and vendors report no independent need.

experiments.hypothesis: Economic operators need vendor-neutral DPP backup independent of their primary provider.
experiments.method: Audit 15 DPP providers and interview 8 operator/PIM owners using a portability-and-failover demo.
experiments.pass: Two operators expose an unsolved continuity requirement and one funds a design pilot.
experiments.kill: Major providers already offer independently hosted, portable, multi-vendor, verifiable continuity at acceptable cost.

experiments.hypothesis: Provider fragmentation creates paid demand beyond C2PA conformance and open-source verification.
experiments.method: Run an authorised multi-provider transformation corpus through real publishing pipelines and interview five publishers.
experiments.pass: Three publishers show repeated undetected mark loss and one pays for cross-provider routing or survival assurance.
experiments.kill: Official/vendor detectors plus C2PA tooling cover the workflow or buyers do not control downstream transformations.
